text:
maya.kapoor: FYI — Acme opened a dispute: Feb invoice shows 1,180,457 embed units billed but our current embed_events table has ~879,223. Looks like the delta matches the recent dedupe/TTL work. Can ops + finance validate?

liam.garcia: ack. customer org? can you paste the query you ran and rough delta calc?

maya.kapoor: customer_id=acme_corp_prod. Quick counts I ran:
```sql
-- raw ingest counts
SELECT count(*) FROM embed_events WHERE customer_id='acme_corp_prod' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28'; -- 1,180,457

-- current (post-dedupe/ttl)
SELECT count(*) FROM embed_events_live WHERE customer_id='acme_corp_prod' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28'; -- 879,223

-- delta ~301,234
```

metering-bot: note: embed-ttl-cleaner job completed 2026-02-28T03:12Z — purged 301,234 rows from embed_events_shard_7

priya.singh: that purge number lines up with the delta. question: billing exports should snapshot before TTL cleanup. did the billing export include duplicates or run before dedupe?

sam.engineering: export_snapshot is populated at 00:15 UTC daily. There is a separate dedupe/ttl pipeline that ran at 03:12 UTC. I pulled export_job logs and saw a retry for shard_7 around 00:18. might explain a race.

liam.garcia: can you paste the export logs for 2026-02-27 night? we need to see if any export retries produced duplicate rows or if dedupe ran against a different table.

sam.engineering: log excerpt:
```
[2026-02-27T00:15:12Z] export-job INFO upload snapshot export_snapshot_2026_02_27 shard_1..shard_10
[2026-02-27T00:18:03Z] export-job WARN shard_7: Failed to upload snapshot: 502 Bad Gateway, retry 1/3
[2026-02-27T00:18:14Z] export-job WARN shard_7: Failed to upload snapshot: 502 Bad Gateway, retry 2/3
[2026-02-27T00:18:29Z] export-job INFO shard_7: upload succeeded after retry
[2026-02-27T03:12:00Z] dedupe-job INFO removed 301,234 duplicate rows from export_snapshot_2026_02_27_shard_7
```

priya.singh: so export succeeded (with duplicates) then dedupe removed rows later. billing pipeline ingested the pre-dedupe snapshot, so billing table has the higher count. current live table shows the post-dedupe state.

maya.kapoor: summary: customer was billed against pre-dedupe numbers (1,180,457) but our canonical live count is 879,223. We need to decide whether to credit the ~301k embeds. Ops, did any of these deduped rows represent legitimate unique requests (idempotency failures)?

sam.engineering: the dedupe keys were request_id + content_hash; analysis shows ~98% exact duplicates (retries). small fraction are true unique (0.6%). Looks safe to treat duplicates as non-billable.

liam.garcia: finance POV: we should credit the difference to keep trust. Need approval from finance lead and a note for process change to avoid future races. Can we compute dollar amount?

maya.kapoor: using standard embed unit price $0.0004 per embed => 301,234 * 0.0004 = $120.49 (rounded). I'll round to $120.50 and prepare credit.

andre.p: I approve issuing the credit of $120.50. Please open FIN ticket and record the audit queries. :white_check_mark:

maya.kapoor: created FIN-4321 — attached queries, logs, and credit calc. Will schedule the credit for next billing cycle and notify Acme. Also filing ops follow-up to change sequencing. cc @sam.engineering

sam.engineering: I'll change export -> 00:15 UTC, then hold dedupe for +48h window; also adding an idempotency check to the export uploader to avoid re-upload duplicates causing inflated snapshots. Will PR the change and add test.

metering-bot: billing-update: scheduled credit for customer acme_corp_prod — 301,234 embed units ($120.50) on next billing run. Ticket FIN-4321 updated.

maya.kapoor: thanks all — closing thread once credit posts.
